stimulus.source_note: Casta painting, 18th century, oil on canvas, public domain; Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: This single canvas gathers sixteen casta paintings, each labeling a different combination of parents and child. The panels run from 'Español con India, Mestizo' to 'Noteentiendo con India, Tornaatras,' covering Spanish, Indigenous, African, and mixed ancestry in every combination.

stem: This single canvas gathers sixteen casta paintings, each labeling a different combination of parents and child. What does the painting's structure show about Spanish colonial society?

options.text: Spanish colonial society formally ranked social status by ancestry amid extensive racial mixing.
The Spanish crown successfully prevented all racial mixing in its colonies.
Enslaved Africans were legally classified as equals of Spanish settlers.
The casta system was created by Native leaders to preserve their own hierarchies.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
